question: Does lexical similarity to revealed questions improve item-level prediction beyond the group mean?
method: Tokenize NFKC-casefolded text into Unicode words, use 1+log(tf), and smooth IDF 1+log((n+1)/(df+1)) fitted only on the current matching revealed prefix. Compute cosine similarity c_i to each acquired item; set w_i=n*(1+c_i)/(n+sum(c)). Predict (1+sum(w_i*y_i))/(n+2). No neighbor truncation or tuned similarity scale.
text_policy: For serialized chat prompts, use the final user message to exclude demonstrations. Otherwise use the supplied item_content string. Empty features yield zero cosine. No item_features, answer keys, traces or model-name features enter prediction.
permutation: For each pair, seed and budget, deterministically shuffle the revealed-label vector using SHA256(pair:seed:budget:retrieval-null-v1) as the random seed. Preserve the label count and success count; reuse exactly the same similarities. One permutation is a diagnostic, not a significance test.
invariants: Total label weight remains n. Budgets zero and one match Beta(1,1) exactly. Equal similarities give the baseline. Only the full eight-field subject and benchmark-matching revealed labels are used.
evaluation: Score each evaluation item separately, and include all its response rows. Reuse the saved item and guarded splits, three acquisition seeds and six budgets. The constant-within-group aggregate shortcut is invalid for this predictor.
screening_rule: Advance only if observed equal-pair and equal-benchmark ALC improve over Beta(1,1), at least four of five benchmark means improve, guarded equal-benchmark direction stays favorable, and each primary acquisition seed's equal-benchmark delta is negative. The real-label predictor must also beat the shuffled-label control in both primary and guarded equal-benchmark means before attributing gain to text. Passing still requires fresh public validation before promotion.
constraints: One fixed lexical weighting rule, no neighbors or scale search; no paid services, external embeddings, downloads or leaderboard calls.
limitations: All five benchmarks were inspected previously; this is development evidence.
Only three fixed acquisition trajectories; no exact expectation or benchmark-level significance claim for this item-dependent predictor.
Words may reflect language, templates or formatting rather than difficulty.
Lexical and source-question guards do not prove full semantic independence.
Large local groups do not reproduce the hosted 1000-pair sample cap.
